summary: Summit lookout; the earliest documented structure is 1942 (some sources say the 1930s), and the two-story R-6 cab dates from 1977. Open to visitors on summer weekends when the road is open.

events.note: First lookout on the summit per NHLR; the 1942 Minidoka forest history quoted by Forest Lookouts Idaho says it was established and maintained through fire season. Other sources say 1930s.
Trailer lookout added, per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; a July 1962 newspaper item reports a trailer house taken to the station
Glen E. Anderson family of Heyburn lived in the trailer and manned the lookout; a 1964 report says they did so the year before
Dave Gillett of Declo took over from Jim Reid, who had been drafted
Outdated buildings and trailer replaced by a $25,000 two-story permanent cab; NHLR and other sources give 1977 as the cab's build year
Jim Sheridan listed as lookout personnel 1985-2007; a 1999 newspaper profile says he spent every summer there for 15 years
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register; the NHLR page gives the registration date as September 27, 2020, and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the first structure to 1942 and the current cab to 1977; the Forest Service, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe a 1930s post. The 1930s date is not backed by a dated primary quote here, so 1942 is the earliest documented year.
firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the trailer lookout to 1960, while the newspaper item we found is from July 1962. The sources do not settle which came first.
NHLR says the lookout is generally staffed during fire season; firelookout.com says sometimes staffed in summer. Both describe seasonal staffing, with no current roster found.

notes_for_editor: Brief's NHLR registration date (Sept 27, 2020) is now confirmed on the NHLR page itself ('Date Registered September 27, 2020'); an earlier note said it was not visible. The brief's 1977 'built' is the current cab; first lookout 1942. The 'climbable' flag was removed: no source says the cab can be climbed, only that it is open to visitors on summer weekends (recorded under access). Location conflict unresolved: NHLR 42.30895,-113.658925 vs Idaho Fire Lookouts 42.31463,-113.6589 (about 630 m apart). Forest Service road-closed status is time-sensitive; recheck before publishing. No specific fire spotted by the lookout was named in the sources read. A September 1942 Burley Herald item on the same page describes a short-wave radio at the summit but names no fire. Staffing as_of is undated across sources. Source 3 bundles several newspaper clippings reprinted on one page; the 1942 history and 1962-1999 items all come from it.
